report.source_text: After the fixation of the cyst in 10% neutral buffered formalin, numerous sections of the tumor were cut for paraffin blocks, and the definitive histopathological diagnosis was serous cystadenofibroma of the ovary (ICD-O 9014/0). The differences between the intraoperative examination report and the formalin-fixed material result from the fact that multiple samples were taken, not just one as during the frozen section. The differentiating factor is the more prominent stromal component present in the formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded samples.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old woman with lifelong obesity presented with massive abdominal distension (circumference 195 cm), left-sided abdominal pain, oligomenorrhea (up to 37 days), infertility, and lower extremity edema. Initial vital signs showed tachycardia (HR 110), tachypnea (RR 25), and hypertension (BP 180/96) secondary to mass effect. Preoperative abdominal ultrasound revealed a massive fluid-filled tumor with segmentally visible solid components, though complete visualization was limited to 24-25 cm due to body habitus. Intraoperative examination identified an 80×50×50 cm multiloculated cyst originating from the left ovary with smooth inner/outer surfaces, wall thickness 3-10 mm, and an 18 cm fallopian tube stretched across its surface; the right adnexa and uterus were normal. Surgical resection involved removal of the tumor wall with partial left oophorectomy. Histopathological examination of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue confirmed serous cystadenofibroma (ICD-O 9014/0), distinguished from intraoperative frozen section by its prominent fibrous stromal component. Postoperative course was uneventful: the patient ambulated on postoperative day 1, Foley catheter removed on day 2, discharged on day 7, and demonstrated complete resolution of symptoms with improved mobility and breathing by 2 weeks.
